summary.text: A polynya is an area of open, unfrozen seawater surrounded by sea ice.
Coastal polynyas are mainly opened by strong winds pushing ice away from the coast, while open-ocean polynyas appear more sporadically in the middle of the ice pack.
Ice forming in coastal polynyas sheds salty brine that sinks, and the light and nutrients in their open water feed blooms that support fish, birds and marine mammals.

items.prompt: Strong winds blow off the Antarctic coast all winter, shoving the sea ice out to sea. What forms along the shore?

options.label: A thick ridge of ice piled against the coast
A solid sheet that stays fixed to the shore
A stretch of open water where new ice keeps forming
An iceberg broken off from the coastline

items.explain: Wind driving ice away from the coast leaves open water, in which new ice forms and is herded off in turn.

items.prompt: Why does plant plankton grow much faster in a polynya than under the surrounding ice?

options.label: More light gets in, and upwelling brings nutrients
The water there is much warmer than tropical seas
Fewer animals live there to eat the plankton
Melting ice pours fresh water full of sugar in

items.explain: Without ice, light reaches deeper into the water, and polynyas are typically tied to upwelling of nutrient-rich water.

items.prompt: Ice forms fast in a coastal polynya off Antarctica, leaving salt behind in the water. Where does that salty water end up?

options.label: It floats on top as a fresh surface layer
It freezes into the new ice above it
It spreads out across the surface sea ice
It sinks to the ocean floor as bottom water

items.explain: Brine rejection makes the seawater saltier, and it sinks to the bottom as Antarctic Bottom Water.

items.prompt: One year, a polynya that usually opens in the Ross Sea stays frozen over. What would you expect for the local seals?

options.label: More seals born, thanks to the extra ice
More seals dying that year
No change, since seals avoid open water
Seals moving onto the frozen polynya

items.explain: Seal mortality rose in years when the Ross Sea Polynya did not open.

items.prompt: In the middle of the pack ice, warm water keeps welling up from below and holds the surface at or above freezing. What happens at the surface?

options.label: Ice grows thicker there than anywhere else
Icebergs collect there from nearby glaciers
Ice forms slowly or not at all, leaving open water
The water turns fresher and freezes faster

items.explain: Warm upwelling that keeps the surface at or above freezing reduces or stops ice production, opening a sensible heat polynya.

items.prompt: A strong polar cyclone settles over the middle of the ice pack. How can it open a polynya?

options.label: Its warm rain melts a hole straight through
Its winds push ice outward away from the centre
Its low pressure lifts the ice off the water
Its winds pile ice into the centre and sink it

items.explain: Cyclonic winds push the ice in opposite directions away from the cyclone's centre, opening the pack.
